lookahead_risk: Low. The decision bar is sig = i1 - 1, the last bar before 12:00 UTC. That is the 11:55 M5 bar: bars are left-closed and labelled by open time (edge/data/resample.py), so its close is the 12:00 price. Every price input comes from bars i0..sig. H and L are m.bid_h[i0:i1].max() and m.bid_l[i0:i1].min(); the slice end is exclusive, so the 12:00 entry bar is never in the window. C is m.bid_c[sig]. ATR is daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, 20)) read as atr[sig]: the mean range of the 20 completed NY trading days before the trading day that contains 12:00 UTC. The 11:55 and 12:00 bars are in the same trading day because the NY roll is at 21:00 or 22:00 UTC. The entry is a market order acted on from bar sig + 1. The only reads past sig are bar existence and timestamps: m.ts[i1] - t1 > max_delay and i1 >= m.n (a fill-bar guard prescribed in the hypothesis-stage notes_for_builder, same convention as the oracle modules), and ix < m.n with the exit flag on ix - 1 (a clock exit known in advance). None of these carry price information. On 2010-2023 data for all six markets the fill guard removed 0 signal days, and no exit bar was more than 15 minutes after 16:00. Truncation, perturbation and determinism probes all passed. Those probes only change prices at two fixed cut points, so I checked the timestamp reads by hand and with the independent re-implementation described in notes.
notes: Verification used read-only scratch scripts on design and check data only (ending 2024-01-01). No P&L or R statistics were computed or looked at. Equivalence: I wrote an independent, timestamp-based implementation of the registered rules, with its own ATR20 from NY-close trading days. At the default cell it reproduced the module's signals exactly on all six markets over 2010-2023: EURUSD 584, GBPUSD 761, USDJPY 308, AUDUSD 319, USDCAD 275 and GBPJPY 702 entries, with 0 differences in signal bar, side, sl_dist (m x R) or exit-flag bar. It also matched exactly at k 0.5 / q 0.15 / m 0.75 on EURUSD 2014-11..2015-12 and GBPJPY 2011-11..2012-12. Every signal is on the 11:55 bar, every fill is at the 12:00 open, and only Monday to Friday trade. Timing: I ran the executor on those two slices and looked at timing only. All entries were at 12:00, all signal exits at the 16:00 open, every trade closed on the same UTC day, executor risk equals sl_dist, and the only exit reasons were SIGNAL and SL. Plumbing: k, q, m, window_start, window_end, exit_utc and max_delay_min are all read from p, and PARAMS equals the spec defaults. The stop multiple is bound to stop_mult, so it does not shadow the Market m. Changing m changes only sl_dist (exactly x1.5); k = 0.8 entries are a subset of k = 0.5, and q = 0.15 entries a subset of q = 0.25. On every entry sl_dist >= m x k x ATR > 0. Weekdays, UTC clock times and the NY-close ATR day are handled correctly. In EURUSD design data no Saturday or Sunday stub trading days feed ATR20, and only 3 of 2,086 trading days have fewer than 100 M5 bars. The fill-bar guard is missing from the hypothesis rules text but appears in the approved hypothesis-stage notes_for_builder and in the module docstring. It removed nothing; the rules record could add it for completeness. Process note for the Director (outside this module): check() in edge/agents/steps.py calls get_market(hyp['stage_a_market'], hyp['timeframe']) with no end date. As a result, dynamic_check's last-150,000-bar sample runs from 2024-10-07 to 2026-10-09, inside the locked holdout, and the checker's 51 entries are holdout-period signal counts. No P&L is computed there, and the pipeline itself cuts markets at holdout_start(). Passing end=holdout_start() in check() would make the lock hold literally.
